summary: The draft discovery brief contains a blocker violation by extensively citing EDA finding IDs (F01-F19), assumption IDs (A1-A4), requirement IDs (R1-R3), and experiment IDs (E1-E2) as citation brackets, contrary to the ground rules. It also has a major overclaim by presenting a word-for-word shared/templated quote across interviews as independent evidence without noting its templated nature.

objections.problem: The brief cites internal identifiers such as EDA finding IDs (F04, F08, F12, F13, F14, F15, F16, F18, F19), assumption IDs (A1-A4), requirement IDs (R1-R3), and experiment IDs (E1-E2) as citation brackets. Ground rules state to cite only valid source IDs (interview turns, whole interviews, competitor rows, and market snippets) and explicitly prohibit citing F01-F19.
objections.fix: Remove all citation brackets containing F, A, R, and E identifiers, and restrict citations exclusively to valid source IDs (e.g., P01:t2, P01, C:MealLoop, S01).

objections.excerpt: such as "Things disappear in the back of the fridge and I find them two weeks later, usually when they're already off." [P01:t2, P08:t2]
objections.problem: The brief cites a sentence that is shared word-for-word between P01 and P08 as independent evidence without flagging it as a templated response, violating F05.
objections.fix: Explicitly note that this sentence is shared across interviews (templated quote) and present raw versus evidence-weighted support counts.
